title: BRICS Declaration: India’s Great U-turn on Iran
author: Asif Ullah Khan
text:
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian being honored at a meeting with a group of Indian religious leaders, intellectuals, and businesspeople in New Delhi, India, on Sept. 11, 2026, the eve of the 18th BRICS Summit.
Credit: X/Iran in India
Before the BRICS summit in New Delhi, political analysts had warned that India would have to do a very difficult tightrope walk given the presence of China, Russia, and Iran. It was a foregone conclusion that they would use this platform for U.S. bashing. With India’s current tug-of-war with the Donald Trump administration, the honchos at South Block (India’s foreign ministry headquarters) used nuanced vocabulary and calibrated the final declaration in such a way that the United States was not named, but the declaration explicitly called for an end to unilateral economic sanctions, protectionist trade measures, and arbitrary tariffs.The surprising outcome of the summit is this: what is being hailed as a triumph of strategic autonomy saw the dilution of India’s foreign policy since the advent of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.[...]
